official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Best Practices for Claude Opus 4.7 with Claude Code
official_anthropic.description: Primary source for Opus 4.7 behavior changes (shipped 2026-04-16): literal instruction following, fewer default subagents, xhigh default reasoning, adaptive thinking replacing budget_tokens, auto-calibrated response length, tokenizer change, positive examples over 'Don't do this'.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: What's New in Claude Opus 4.8
official_anthropic.description: Primary source for Opus 4.8 (shipped 2026-05-28, model id claude-opus-4-8): effort default is now 'high' on all surfaces including Claude Code (not xhigh); mid-conversation system messages preserve prompt cache; 1M context by default; better compaction recovery and tool triggering; budget_tokens still returns 400; lower 1,024-token cache minimum.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Claude Opus 4.7 Prompting Guide
official_anthropic.description: Official prompting guidance referenced by the 4.7 best-practices blog. Adaptive thinking, intent-first prompting, and tool-use patterns.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
official_anthropic.description: Primary source: Claude Sonnet 5 (shipped 2026-06-30) supersedes the Opus 4.7/4.8 line as the default Claude Code model; effort still defaults to `high` (verified via the Sonnet 5 prompting guide below), same as Opus 4.8 — the 4.8 migration checklist's effort guidance carries forward unchanged.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Prompting Claude Sonnet 5
official_anthropic.description: Confirms effort defaults to `high` on Sonnet 5 (same as Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8); raise to `xhigh` for the hardest coding/agentic tasks.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
official_anthropic.description: Primary source: Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 (shipped 2026-06-09, global availability from 2026-07-01) is Anthropic's newest generation, above the Opus 4.x line. 1M-token default context window — raises the temptation to skip external memory/retrieval; this skill's progressive-disclosure discipline applies more, not less, at this scale.

official_anthropic.name: Anthropic: Prompting Claude Fable 5
official_anthropic.description: Confirms adaptive thinking remains the only thinking mode on Fable 5/Mythos 5 (`budget_tokens` still rejected); thinking depth is driven by the effort parameter and query complexity, not a memory-file setting.

community_guides.name: forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills
community_guides.description: MIT-licensed Karpathy-inspired behavioral-rules plugin. Source for goal-transformation pattern, trace test, 200-line rewrite heuristic, orphan-vs-pre-existing dead code distinction, tradeoff disclosure framing, and working-if success metric. Derivative of Karpathy's public observations on LLM coding pitfalls.
patterns_merged: M1: goal transformation (Transform Vague Tasks to Verifiable Goals)
M2: working-if success metric (Measuring Whether Memory Is Working)
M3: trace test (Every changed line must trace directly to the user's request)
M5: orphan vs pre-existing dead code distinction
karpathy_quotes_cited: The models make wrong assumptions on your behalf and just run along with them without checking.
They really like to overcomplicate code and APIs, bloat abstractions, don't clean up dead code.
LLMs are exceptionally good at looping until they meet specific goals... give it success criteria.

community_guides.name: garrytan/gstack
community_guides.description: MIT-licensed Garry Tan / Y Combinator AI-engineering workflow skill pack. Source for the completeness-maximalism operating mode: compression-ratio framing (human-team time vs. AI-assisted time by task type), the boil-the-ocean completeness heuristic, the three-layer search-before-building knowledge model, and the destructive-command safe-exceptions allowlist pattern. Companion contract to coding-behavior.md's defensive-minimalism mode, not a merge into it.
patterns_merged: M1: compression-ratio table reframed as time-savings justification for completeness
M2: boil-the-ocean completeness heuristic (prefer the full implementation when the marginal cost is small)
M3: three-layer knowledge model for search-before-building (established pattern / current trend / reasoned from the problem)
M4: safe-exceptions allowlist pattern for otherwise-forbidden destructive operations
M5: user-sovereignty framing (two models agreeing is signal, not a mandate to act unprompted)
garry_tan_quotes_cited: The marginal cost of completeness is near zero with AI. Do the whole thing.
The answer is the finished product, not a plan to build it.
